text: {"decision":"GO","artifact":{"author":"Graham Hill","audience":"Business and IT leaders","format":"Frozen editorial outline; not a drafted post","thesis":{"type":"Editorial inference","text":"Successful access alone does not establish payment authorization: payout decisions need evidence of an approved obligation, beneficiary and amount, and evidence that the execution path enforces those conditions.","sources":["CIAD-2026-0046","CIAD-2026-0058"]},"reader_consequence":{"type":"Proposed operating arrangement","text":"The business owner defines what authorizes a payout; the technical owner supplies evidence that each fund-movement path enforces those requirements. Together they determine which paths may operate, require review or remain held when authorization or remediation evidence is missing."},"load_bearing_facts":[{"id":"F1","text":"CERT-In reports that attackers invoked fund-transfer APIs directly using valid credentials from victims’ whitelisted infrastructure, bypassing application-level checks. Transactions included dummy references with no corresponding records.","sources":["CIAD-2026-0046"]},{"id":"F2","text":"CERT-In’s follow-up advisory reports renewed attacks after incomplete remediation, as well as movement from non-production to production through shared credentials, tokens or network paths.","sources":["CIAD-2026-0058"]}],"necessary_qualification":"These reports support an evidence requirement, not a finding that any particular organization is exposed or ready to resume payouts; local authorization, enforcement and remediation evidence is still required.","narrative_beats":[{"beat":1,"purpose":"Establish the authorization gap","content":"Open with CERT-In’s reported combination of accepted credentials, whitelisted infrastructure and transaction references lacking corresponding records.","fact_ids":["F1"]},{"beat":2,"purpose":"Make the business consequence concrete","content":"Ask what approved obligation, beneficiary and amount justify the payout. Present these as proposed decision requirements, not evidence already available locally.","type":"Editorial inference"},{"beat":3,"purpose":"Define the technical handoff","content":"Require evidence that relevant execution paths enforce the agreed authorization conditions, and that suspected compromise has been investigated. Under the proposed policy, it is held for review until authorization can be established.","type":"Hypothetical illustration; not a reported event"},{"beat":5,"purpose":"Close on the shared decision","content":"The useful handoff is the business definition of an authorized payment paired with technical evidence that the payment path enforces it.","type":"Editorial conclusion"}]},"claim_support":[{"claim_id":"F1","type":"Reported fact","sources":["CIAD-2026-0046"],"locations":["Description","Key TTPs Observed"]},{"claim_id":"F2","type":"Reported fact","sources":["CIAD-2026-0058"],"locations":["Overview","Description"]},{"claim":"Access alone is insufficient evidence of payment authorization; decisions should connect approved payment records to enforcement across execution paths.","type":"Editorial inference and proposed decision requirement","sources":["CIAD-2026-0046","CIAD-2026-0058"],"locations":["Description","Recommended Actions"]},{"claim":"Role allocation, operating decisions and the illustrative payout hold are proposed or hypothetical.","type":"Explicit proposal or illustration","sources":[]}],"limitations":["Only supplied material was used; sources were not independently retrieved or verified.","The CERT-In advisories form one reporting chain; the follow-up is not independent corroboration.","Recommended safeguards are not demonstrated outcomes or guarantees of control effectiveness.","No organization-specific evidence or confirmed allocation of owner responsibilities was supplied.","This freezes an editorial outline only; no post has been drafted, published or forwarded."]}
